'''Alan Travis Williams''' (born January 28, 1993) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Nagoya Diamond Dolphins]] of the Japanese [[B.League]]. He played college basketball for [[UC Santa Barbara Gauchos men's basketball|UC Santa Barbara]] before beginning his professional career with the [[Qingdao DoubleStar|Qingdao DoubleStar Eagles]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] in 2015.

==High school career==
Williams attended [[North High School (Phoenix, Arizona)|North High School]]. After playing in just one game as a freshman and averaging just 3.5 points as a sophomore, Williams averaged 12.5 points, 10.9 rebounds and 3.3 blocks per game as a junior in 2009–10.<ref>[http://www.maxpreps.com/athlete/alan-williams/D2WDJ_TrEeKZ5AAmVebBJg/gendersport/basketball-stats.htm Alan Williams' Basketball Stats – MaxPreps]</ref> As a senior in 2010–11, he averaged 22.1 points, 16.2 rebounds, 4.5 blocks, 2.0 steals, and 1.5 assists, leading North to a Metro Region championship and the Class 5A quarterfinals. He was named Arizona State Player of the Year that season.<ref name="bio">{{cite web|url=http://ucsbgauchos.com/sports/m-baskbl/2014-15/bios/williams_alan_8we9|title=UCSB bio|work=UCSBGauchos.com|access-date=March 17, 2016|archive-date=March 16, 2016|archive-url=https://archive.today/20160316115059/http://ucsbgauchos.com/sports/m-baskbl/2014-15/bios/williams_alan_8we9|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==College career==
Williams played four seasons of college basketball for [[UC Santa Barbara Gauchos men's basketball|UC Santa Barbara]] between 2011 and 2015, finishing his career as the Gauchos' all-time leader in rebounds and second all-time leading scorer. As a junior in 2013–14, he was named the [[Big West Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big West Conference Player of the Year]]. He also earned first-team All-[[Big West Conference|Big West]] honors as a sophomore, junior, and senior, and led the NCAA in rebounding as a junior and senior.<ref name="bio" /><ref name="China">{{cite web|url=http://ucsbgauchos.com/sports/m-baskbl/2015-16/releases/20150728sfkxzc|title=Alan Williams Signs Deal to Play Professionally in China|work=UCSBGauchos.com|date=July 28, 2015|access-date=March 8, 2016|archive-date=March 9, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160309001300/http://ucsbgauchos.com/sports/m-baskbl/2015-16/releases/20150728sfkxzc|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 112 games (101 starts) over his four-year career, Williams averaged 15.5 points, 10.0 rebounds, 1.0 assists, 1.0 steals and 1.9 blocks in 27.0 minutes per game.<ref name="bio" /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://stats.washingtonpost.com/cbk/players.asp?id=110293|title=#15 Alan Williams|work=WashingtonPost.com|access-date=March 8, 2016}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===2015 NBA Summer League===
After going undrafted in the [[2015 NBA draft]], Williams played for the [[Charlotte Hornets]] (three games in Orlando) and [[Houston Rockets]] (four games in Las Vegas) during the [[2015 NBA Summer League]]. For his play with the Rockets in Las Vegas, he earned All-NBA Summer League Second Team honors.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/kyle-anderson-named-2015-nba-summer-league-mvp|title=Kyle Anderson Named 2015 NBA Summer League MVP|work=NBA.com|date=July 19, 2015|access-date=March 8, 2016}}</ref>

===Qingdao DoubleStar Eagles (2015–2016)===
On July 25, 2015, Williams signed a one-year deal with the [[Qingdao DoubleStar|Qingdao DoubleStar Eagles]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].<ref name="China" /><ref>{{cite web|last=Charania|first=Shams|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/238863/Alan-Williams-Signs-One-Year-Deal-With-Qingdao-In-China|title=Alan Williams Signs One-Year Deal With Qingdao In China|work=RealGM.com|date=July 25, 2015|access-date=March 8, 2016}}</ref> He appeared in 35 of the team's 38 games during the 2015–16 season, as the Eagles missed a playoff berth with a 16–22 win–loss record. Over those 35 games, he averaged 20.8 points, a league-leading 15.4 rebounds, 2.1 assists, 1.3 steals and 1.6 blocks per game.<ref name=azcentral>{{cite web|last=Coro|first=Paul|url=http://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2016/03/07/suns-sign-phoenix-native-alan-williams-10-day/81452936/|title=Suns to sign Phoenix native Alan Williams to 10-day contract|work=AZCentral.com|date=March 7, 2016|access-date=March 8, 2016}}</ref>

===Phoenix Suns (2016–2018)===
[[File:Alan Williams (31133352066).jpg|thumb|Williams playing for the Suns in 2016]]
On March 8, 2016, Williams signed a 10-day contract with the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-sign-alan-williams|title=Suns Sign Alan Williams|work=NBA.com|date=March 8, 2016|access-date=March 8, 2016}}</ref> He made his NBA debut on March 17 during a 103–69 loss to the [[Utah Jazz]], recording one point and one steal in two minutes.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160317/PHXUTA/gameinfo.html|title=Ingles scores 15, Jazz beat Suns 103-69|work=NBA.com|date=March 17, 2016|access-date=March 17, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160621003531/http://www.nba.com/games/20160317/PHXUTA/gameinfo.html|archive-date=June 21, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> The following day, he signed a multi-year deal with the Suns.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-sign-alan-williams-multi-year-contract|title=Suns Sign Alan Williams to Multi-Year Contract|work=NBA.com|date=March 18, 2016|access-date=March 18, 2016}}</ref> On April 9, he recorded a then season-high seven rebounds in a 121–100 win over the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160409/PHXNOP/gameinfo.html|title=Goodwin, Teletovic lead Suns over Pelicans 121-100|work=NBA.com|date=April 9, 2016|access-date=April 10, 2016}}</ref> In the Suns' season finale on April 13, Williams recorded his first double-double in the NBA with season highs of 14 points and 12 rebounds (alongside 3 blocks) in a 114–105 win over the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160413/LACPHX/gameinfo.html|title=Teletovic's 22 leads Suns past Clippers reserves, 114-105|work=NBA.com|date=April 13, 2016|access-date=April 14, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160417140820/http://www.nba.com/games/20160413/LACPHX/gameinfo.html|archive-date=April 17, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Brooklyn/Long Island Nets (2018–2019)===
On September 24, 2018, Williams signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Brooklyn Nets]]. Under the terms of the deal, he split his time between Brooklyn and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Long Island Nets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2018/09/24/brooklyn-nets-sign-alan-williams-to-two-way-contract|title=BROOKLYN NETS SIGN ALAN WILLIAMS TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT|work=NBA.com|date=September 24, 2018|access-date=January 2, 2019}}</ref> He was waived by Brooklyn on January 2, 2019,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2019/01/02/nets-waive-alan-williams|title=NETS WAIVE ALAN WILLIAMS|work=NBA.com|date=January 2, 2019|access-date=January 2, 2019}}</ref> but was then re-signed to another two-way contract on January 11.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2019/01/11/nets-sign-alan-williams|title=Nets sign Alan Williams|work=NBA.com|date=January 11, 2019|access-date=January 11, 2019}}</ref> He made his NBA debut that night<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071300|title=Leonard has 20 points, 11 rebounds, Raptors top Nets 122-105|work=ESPN.com|date=January 11, 2019|access-date=January 11, 2019}}</ref> and remained with the team for the rest of the 2018–19 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/willial03/gamelog/2019|title=Alan Williams 2018-19 Game Log|work=basketball-reference.com|access-date=August 5, 2022}}</ref>

===Shaanxi Xinda (2019)===
In July and August 2019, Williams played with [[Shaanxi Wolves|Shaanxi Xinda]] of the [[National Basketball League (China)|Chinese NBL]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Alan Williams signs at Shaanxi Xinda|url=https://www.asia-basket.com/China/news/585257/Alan-Williams-signs-at-Shaanxi-Xinda|date=July 5, 2019|website=asia-basket.com|access-date=July 5, 2019}}</ref>

===Lokomotiv Kuban (2019–2022)===
On August 13, 2019, Williams signed with [[PBC Lokomotiv-Kuban|Lokomotiv Kuban]] of the [[VTB United League]] for the 2019–20 season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/lokomotiv-kuban-signs-alan-williams/|title=Lokomotiv Kuban signs Alan Williams
|date=August 13, 2019|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=August 14, 2019}}</ref>

On June 4, 2020, Williams re-signed with Lokomotiv Kuban for the 2020–21 season.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Carchia |first1=Emiliano |title=Lokomotiv Kuban re-signs Alan Williams |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/lokomotiv-kuban-re-signs-alan-williams/ |website=Sportando |access-date=June 4, 2020 |date=June 4, 2020}}</ref> In November 2020, he was ruled out for the rest of the season with a knee injury.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lokomotiv's Williams out for the season|url=https://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/b4xsqgfbimst6bjv/lokomotiv-s-williams-out-for-the-season|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210125001825/https://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/b4xsqgfbimst6bjv/lokomotiv-s-williams-out-for-the-season|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 25, 2021|date=November 24, 2020|website=eurocupbasketball.com|access-date=November 24, 2020}}</ref>

Williams returned to Lokomotiv Kuban for the 2021–22 season but left the team in March 2022.<ref>{{cite web|title=Alan Williams leaves Lokomotiv Kuban Krasnodar|url=https://basketnews.com/news-168103-alan-williams-leaves-lokomotiv-kuban-krasnodar.html|date=March 16, 2022|website=basketnews.com|access-date=August 5, 2022}}</ref>

===S.E. Melbourne Phoenix (2022–2023)===
On August 5, 2022, Williams signed with the [[South East Melbourne Phoenix]] in Australia for the [[2022–23 NBL season]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Welcome to the Phoenix: Alan Williams|url=https://www.semphoenix.com.au/news/welcome-to-the-phoenix-alan-williams|date=August 5, 2022|website=semphoenix.com.au|access-date=August 5, 2022}}</ref> He led the league in rebounding with 9.6 per game.<ref name=re-sign>{{cite web|title=Alan Williams Re-Signs with Phoenix for 2 More Years|url=https://www.semphoenix.com.au/news/alan-williams-re-signs-with-phoenix-for-2-more-years|date=February 7, 2023|website=semphoenix.com.au|access-date=February 7, 2023}}</ref>

===Nagoya Diamond Dolphins (2023)===
Following the NBL season, he joined the [[Nagoya Diamond Dolphins]] of the Japanese [[B.League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Alan Williams（アラン・ウィリアムズ）選手 B.LEAGUE2022-23 SEASON契約締結のお知らせ|url=https://nagoya-dolphins.jp/news/detail/id=16896|date=March 6, 2023|website=nagoya-dolphins.jp|access-date=March 18, 2023|language=Japanese}}</ref>

===S.E. Melbourne Phoenix (2023–2024)===
Williams returned to the Phoenix for the [[2023–24 NBL season]] on a two-year deal,<ref name="re-sign" /> but missed the start of the season with a knee injury.<ref>{{cite web|title=Phoenix Star Set to Spend Time on the Sidelines|url=https://www.semphoenix.com.au/news/phoenix-star-set-to-spend-time-on-the-sidelines|date=September 9, 2023|website=semphoenix.com.au|access-date=September 11, 2023}}</ref> He went on to average a league-leading 10.9 rebounds per game before being ruled out for the rest of the season on January 19, 2024, with another knee injury.<ref>{{cite web|title=Williams Ruled Out of NBL24 Regular Season|url=https://www.semphoenix.com.au/news/williams-ruled-out-of-nbl24-regular-season|date=January 19, 2024|website=semphoenix.com.au|access-date=January 19, 2024}}</ref> On March 7, 2024, it was announced that Williams and the Phoenix agreed to mutually terminate his remaining contract.<ref>{{cite web |title=Williams and Phoenix part ways |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/williams-and-phoenix-part-ways |website=NBL |access-date=March 7, 2024 |date=March 7, 2024}}</ref>

===Goyang Sono Skygunners (2024–2025)===
On June 12, 2024, Williams signed with the [[Goyang Sono Skygunners]] of the [[Korean Basketball League]].<ref>{{cite web |title='소노의 에어컨 리그는 뜨겁다' 강력한 외인확보, NBA 피닉스 선즈 출신 빅맨 앨런 윌리엄스 영입 |url=https://www.chosun.com/sports/basketball/2024/06/12/7X4TB4UQ7VL3FXKSIB5ZOV6M7E/ |publisher=조선일보 |access-date=August 31, 2024 |date=June 12, 2024}}</ref> His contract would expire on December 22, replacing by [[Alpha Kaba]].<ref>{{cite web |title=소노, 208cm 카바 영입…윌리엄스는 18일 고별전 예정 |url=https://jumpball.co.kr/news/newsview.php?ncode=1065596166644265 |website=점프볼 |access-date=December 16, 2024 |date=December 16, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=윙스팬 227cm 외국 선수가 성탄절 선물 안길까... 소노, 윌리엄스 대체로 알파 카바 영입 |url=https://www.rookie.co.kr/news/articleView.html?idxno=104356 |website=ROOKIE |access-date=December 16, 2024 |date=December 16, 2024}}</ref> On February 12, 2025, Williams re-signed with the Goyang Sono Skygunners to replace Alpha Kaba.<ref>{{cite web |title='Comeback KBL' 소노, 앨런 윌리엄스 영입 공식 발표…26일 KCC전 출전 예정 |url=https://jumpball.co.kr/news/newsview.php?ncode=1065592661119487 |website=점프볼 |access-date=February 12, 2025 |date=February 12, 2025}}</ref>

===Second stint with Nagoya Diamond Dolphins (2025–present)===
On May 29, 2025, Williams signed with the Nagoya Diamond Dolphins of the Japanese B.League.<ref>{{cite web |title=アラン・ウィリアムズ選手 B.LEAGUE 2025-26 SEASON契約合意（新規）のお知らせ |url=https://nagoya-dolphins.jp/news/detail/id=19815 |website=名古屋ダイヤモンドドルフィンズ |access-date=May 29, 2025 |date=May 29, 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Williams' father, Cody Sr., is a [[Justice of the Peace]] for [[Maricopa County, Arizona|Maricopa County]]. He served on the Phoenix City Council from 1994 to 2002.<ref name="azcentral" /><ref name="abcd">{{cite web|last=Coro|first=Paul|url=http://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2016/11/23/phoenix-suns-alan-williams-family-thankful-for-dream-jobs/94238676/|title=Phoenix Suns' Alan Williams, family thankful for dream jobs|work=AZCentral.com|date=November 23, 2016|access-date=November 23, 2016}}</ref> while his mother, Jeri, is the former [[Chief of Police]] in Phoenix.<ref>{{cite web|last=Spar|first=Jerry|url=http://greenstreet.weei.com/sports/boston/basketball/celtics/2015/06/09/nba-draft-prospect-profile-uc-santa-barbara-cpf-alan-williams/|title=NBA DRAFT PROSPECT PROFILE: UC SANTA BARBARA C/PF ALAN WILLIAMS|work=GreenStreet.weei.com|date=June 9, 2015|access-date=March 8, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160308123923/http://greenstreet.weei.com/sports/boston/basketball/celtics/2015/06/09/nba-draft-prospect-profile-uc-santa-barbara-cpf-alan-williams/|archive-date=March 8, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Cassidy|first1=Megan|last2=Gardiner|first2=Dustin|url=http://www.azcentral.com/story/news/local/phoenix/2016/07/13/jeri-williams-named-new-phoenix-police-chief/87043798/|title=Phoenix makes history with hire of female police chief|work=azcentral.com|date=July 13, 2016|access-date=July 15, 2016}}</ref> His younger brother, Coady Jr., also attended college in Santa Barbara.<ref name="abcd" />
